name: Fester

facts.text: Level 64, 30,000 health, crowd-control immune, armour factor 350 with 20% absorb; resists 20% of melee and 30% of everything else.

35% of its hits give an undiseased target a 120 s disease. Fester's Venom: 80 matter every 4 s for 20 s to everyone within 600 of its target ('An acidic cloud surrounds you!'), 3 s cast, recast 20-30 s, cast when its target is not poisoned.
It walks home at full health when nobody is left on its aggro list; respawn is the epic-encounter interval.
Fester as the rot of the banks when the cattle went, the black reeds and the mire's custom are Living Server writing.

story:
Where the lake drains away west of the hills into a mire, the reeds are black and the air is sour, and Fester lives in it. The old men of Barfog say it was a sickness before it was a creature. When the lady of the lake called her white cattle home, nothing clean grazed the banks any more, and the banks began to rot: first the grass, then the reeds, then the water that ran out of the lake to the west. The rot gathered in the mire. Somewhere, sometime in the years after, it learned to walk.

It is a sickness still, the hill folk say, only one with legs. Whoever it strikes takes the sickness away with him in his blood, a slow sickness that makes every wound close late and every hand that tries to close it work twice as hard. And when it is angry it breathes, and the breath is a sour cloud that clings and burns, and does not stay on the one it breathes at but spreads to everyone standing near him, so that a knot of men round one sick man all burn together. The bwgan of the western ridge, who have to live near the mire, will not gather in threes or fours when Fester is about; they stand apart, each alone, and the old men of Barfog say the bwgan are not as stupid as they look.

It cannot be charmed or held. The druids who used to come up from the south to bless the lake tried once to bind it, the village remembers, and their binding slid off it as water slides off the black reeds.

Twr ap Alsig has a theory that Fester will stop when the cattle come back, because the cattle were what kept the banks clean. The old men say the cattle are not coming back, and that if they did, the first thing they would eat is the mire.
legend: Fester, level 64, 30k, in the black-reed mire west of the lake. Two problems. First, 35% of its hits give the target a 2 minute disease, which cuts healing, so cure disease on the tank every time. Second, Fester's Venom is an acid DoT, 80 every 4 seconds for 20 seconds, that hits everyone within 600 of its target, so everyone who does not need to be near the tank spreads well away from the tank. It recasts every 20 to 30 seconds. It cannot be mezzed or stunned, and has no adds. A wipe resets it to full; it respawns about an hour after death.

aggro: The black reeds part. Something sour rises.
A wet breath, and the air turns.

phases.text: Fester breathes, and the cloud spreads.

death: The mire sinks back into itself.
The sour air begins to clear.

lairEntry: The air is sour. The reeds are black.
Even the bwgan stand apart here.

loremasterTopic.text: The rot that set into Llyn Barfog's banks when the white cattle went home, gathered in the black-reed mire to the west, and learned to walk. Its sickness slows every wound's closing, and its sour breath spreads to everyone near the one it breathes on.

bookPage: From the Barfog Book of Twr ap Alsig. Of the mire. When I was a boy the water that ran west out of the lake was clear, and we took eels from it. Then it went brown, then the reeds went black, then the eels went, and then Fester stood up out of it. The bwgan who live on the western ridge stand apart from each other when it is about, every one alone, never in threes or fours. I used to laugh at them. A company from Camelot went down to the mire last spring and stood together round their sick man, close, the way friends do. They came home coughing, all of them, and the sick man first. I do not laugh at the bwgan now.
